80m activity — rolling 30-minute window

Spots to/from FN32 ± 1 grid square, 83.3 days pooled by UTC time of day (2026-06-03 07:30:00 .. 2026-08-25 15:52:00). Azimuthal equidistant centered on K1TTT (FN32LL): bearing reads straight off the map, distance is radial, and the dashed orange rings are the WW Digi point steps (3000 km). The 30-minute window slides 1 minute per frame, 1440 frames looping the day from 1200Z to 1200Z (the contest clock); the clock shows the window's center. Each active square is drawn at its true 2°×1° footprint and colored on a heat ramp by log spot count (normalized to the day's busiest square) raised to the contrast exponent γ — default 2.5, slider below; γ=1 is the bare log, and the linear toggle swaps the log for v/vmax (the drawn windows span ~4 dex, so linear shows only where the volume is). The raw day/night swing is real: 15m Europe runs 50–60× between its afternoon peak and 03Z. Shading is drawn for the contest date (29–30 Aug): a light band from sunset to the end of nautical twilight (sun 12° down), full night beyond, with the sun at the subsolar point. Auroral ovals are the nominal Kp≈2 extent (66–74° geomagnetic).
